## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dhanapālaseṭṭhipetavatthu* ("The Rich Man Dhanapāla", Pv 19) is a verse narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text illustrates the grim karmic consequences experienced by those who fail to practice generosity and who revile those who do [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify passage-level correspondences with two other stories in the *Petavatthu*: *Khallāṭiyapetivatthu* (Pv 10) and *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus confirms both alignments, registering high textual overlap between segments 13.1–16.4 of Pv 19 and Pv 10 (§12.1–15.4), as well as between segments 13.1–15.4 and Pv 38 (§36.1–38.4) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records substantial Pali-internal text reuse with other *Petavatthu* narratives, including *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31), *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13), *Gaṇapetavatthu* (Pv 45), *Saṭṭhikūṭapetavatthu* (Pv 51), and *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15), as well as shared verses with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Petakopadesa* (Pe 2), and the *Devadūtasutta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.36) [DharmaNexus].
SuttaCentral further notes thematic or verse relationships with numerous canonical and non-Pali works, such as the *Bālapaṇḍitasutta* (MN 129), *Devadūtasutta* (MN 130), *Dhammapada* (Dhp 337), *Theragāthā* (Thag 6.5), *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 20.3), the Niddesa treatises, the *Saṅkiccajātaka* (Ja 530), the Chinese *Dharmapada* (T 210.32), and the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 3) [SuttaCentral]. Cross-language machine matches also align segments of the text with the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
